text: Data: a practice sky (simulation). The two pictures show the same color, so the comparison is fair (score 98 of 100). The color difference alone makes the star look 0.0 percent brighter. The pictures show it 31.6 percent fainter. A real change remains after the color effect is removed. The position measurements say: it stays in place. The motion is 0.02 plus or minus 0.01 arcseconds per year, from 65 pictures. In the later visit the star is 35 percent fainter on average. The change depends on color. Summary: variable source candidate. This is a candidate label and not a discovery.
